sources.title: Kyoto City: Historical chronology
sources.note: Directly read medieval/early Edo chronology: 1467 Onin War; 1573 Ashikaga expulsion; 1582 Nobunaga death; 1600 Sekigahara; 1603 Ieyasu shogun and Okuni performance. Imported map bounds checked separately.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Momoyama Period, 1573-1615
sources.note: Directly read institutional essay: three unifiers, elite artistic patronage, Korean invasions and international exchange. Does not adopt introductory simplification implying provincial warfare began only in the 1560s.

sources.title: Hideyoshi: Collection of Swords, 1588; David J. Lu translation via Columbia Asia for Educators
sources.note: Direct two-page primary-document translation read, especially edict clauses 1-3 and contextual commentary. Same edited work Japan: A Documentary History is used for 1615 military laws in existing Tokugawa card; cumulative work count checked separately. Edict is an intended policy, not proof every farmer was immediately disarmed.

sources.title: Victoria and Albert Museum: Japan’s encounter with Europe, 1573-1853
sources.note: Directly read sixteenth/early seventeenth century section: 1543 Portuguese firearms, production, and 1600-1630 screen as Kyoto imaginative work. Does not adopt broad claims about all Christians or later-century artefacts.

sources.title: Sakai City: Sakai moated urban archaeological site
sources.note: Direct Japanese municipal archaeology account read: late Muromachi to early Edo site, 1615 fire and expanded town plan, layered roads with drains, sixteenth-century tile-lined wells, buried jar latrines near roads with fertilizer collection explicitly proposed.

sources.title: Ichijodani Asakura Family Site Museum: Sengoku Gourmet of Ichijodani, 2024 exhibition leaflet
sources.note: Direct two-page original museum PDF read. Page 2 captions identify red sea bream knife marks, charred rice, repurposed oshiki tray as chopping board, cooking implements and mass-produced ordinary lacquer bowls. This is a distinct 2024 research exhibition, not the existing Muromachi card’s general site/walk pages.

sources.title: Agency for Cultural Affairs: Hideyoshi autograph letter to Kita no Mandokoro, 1593
sources.note: Direct record read. Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum object, Bunroku 2 fifth-month twenty-second day. Content includes diplomacy, orders in Korea, his cold, and concern for wife One over Yodo-dono’s pregnancy. Dates expressed as Japanese document date, not converted Gregorian May 22. No medical efficacy inferred.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Himeji-jo
sources.note: Direct description and OUV read: early seventeenth-century wood architecture, white plaster earthen walls, keep/gates/defence complex. Conflicting 82/83 building totals omitted.

sources.title: Osaka Castle Museum: Toyotomi Stone Wall Museum leaflet
sources.note: Direct two-page museum PDF read: 1583 construction, 1598 Hideyoshi death, 1615 fall, 1620 rebuilding, 1984 wall discovery. Page 2 describes approximately six metres of fill at nakanodan, buried original walls; page 1 tsumenomaru family quarters. English extraction has reversed word order but indexed original preserves text; bounded facts corroborate official museum 2019 leaflet.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art: Black Raku Tea Bowl, object 17.118.74
sources.note: Direct museum object page read: early seventeenth century, hand-moulded lightweight earthenware, indoor kilns, opaque black glaze. Tentative Chojiro attribution and Rikyu legend deliberately not treated as firm object authorship.

sources.title: Printing Museum Tokyo: Saga edition of Tsurezuregusa, object 03793
sources.note: Direct Japanese museum record read: from 1608, wooden movable type joining two to four characters, kanji and hiragana, artistic covers/paper/illustrations, Honami Koetsu and Suminokura Soan. Older literary work reprinted, not authored in seventeenth century.

sources.title: National Archives of Japan: Tales of Ise, Saga edition, 1608
sources.note: Direct object description read. 1608 illustrated vernacular classic; based on Fujiwara Teika’s 1234 copy made for granddaughter. Uses original object/exhibition evidence, not inferred mass literacy.

sources.title: Nagahama Castle History Museum: Nobunaga letter to Tohachi, object B00HCC02
sources.note: Direct Japanese and companion English /en/digital-museum/20 records read. Japanese catalogue precisely dates Eiroku 11 second month (1568), English only broad 1558-1570; original Japanese date preferred. Rice-field confirmation, unknown recipient details, seal 天下布武. English gloss establishing military presence in the territory; museum explains debate over extent of tenka. Both language pages count as one work.

proposedOverrides.name: Japan: Warring States and Unification
proposedOverrides.summary: Regional warfare and unification, followed by early Tokugawa rule, with urban archaeology, crafts and household life.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact missing indexed record only. Existing muromachi, tokugawa-shogunate and japan-1783 are separate narrative phases. No aliases attached and no modern Japanese territory presumed.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Two identical HB multipolygons, world-1530 and world-1600, span 1530-1600 and 1600-1650. Bbox [129.3439,30.8881,141.9980,41.4419]. Main-island outline excludes Hokkaido; it represents neither separate daimyo borders nor unchanged unified government. Public opening makes both limitations explicit.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Imported 1530-1650 retained as map coverage. Civil wars began earlier; 1573 Ashikaga expulsion, 1600 Sekigahara, 1603 Tokugawa shogunate and 1615 Osaka are distinct transitions. The 1615-1650 section is early Edo continuation, not continued nationwide Warring States conflict.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Nagahama museum B00HCC02, Japanese catalogue dates Eiroku 11 second month (1568), while English field is a broad Eiroku-era range. Same object’s Japanese text verifies 天下布武, English supplies translation and debate over tenka. Modern type/romanization explicitly distinguished from original seal script.
batchIdentityNotes.scope: Local food and sanitation evidence tied to Ichijodani and Sakai. Cold and family concerns concern a specific Hideyoshi letter, not ordinary universal medicine. Family castle quarters do not imply simultaneous occupation. Classic text first composed earlier; 1608 printed edition is the contemporary object. No nationwide schooling, literacy or sanitation rate inferred.
